test_title: SSC CHSL Exam 2023 Tier-II Official Paper (Held On: 10 Jan, 2024 Shift 1).
subject: general
question: Which is NOT a Directive Principle to be followed by the State for policy - making?

options.text: Tender age of children is not abused
The operation of economic system results for concentration of wealth
The ownership of material resources of the community are for common good

solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government.
 
• They are included in Part IV of the Constitution of India and aim to create social and economic conditions under which citizens can lead a good life.
 
• **Option 3: "The operation of economic system results for concentration of wealth" is NOT a Directive Principle.**
 
• Other options such as ensuring the tender age of children is not abused, equal pay for equal work, and the ownership of material resources of the community being for the common good, are part of the Directive Principles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Directive Principles are non-justiciable in nature, meaning they are not legally enforceable by the courts for their violation.
 
• They are considered fundamental in the governance of the country and aim to establish a just society in India.
 
• Examples of Directive Principles include the promotion of international peace and security, the organization of village panchayats, and the provision of free legal aid.
 
• These principles act as a yardstick in the hands of the electorate to measure the performance of the government.
